run.question: Fetch me the logs for the inventory-service pod in namespace app-102

report.summary: The pod exists and its logs were retrieved. Kubernetes shows exactly two pods in namespace app-102: inventory-service-7ff7d5959f-vlqgl (Running, containers inventory-service and promtail) and loki-66445c6d6f-pj6sf. Direct container-log retrieval from the inventory-service pod over the sampled hour 2026-11-23T17:50:46Z to 2026-11-23T18:50:46Z returned only 8 promtail sidecar start-up lines and zero lines on the inventory-service container's own stdout stream (current instance 0 lines; no previous instance exists). The application itself writes to /var/log/inventory.log, and the Loki stream with labels job="inventory-service", namespace="app-102", pod_name="inventory-service-7ff7d5959f-vlqgl" returned 8 application lines for that pod between 2026-11-23T18:50:11.885Z and 2026-11-23T18:50:44.414Z: three INFO "Inventory check completed - all systems operational" lines, an INFO reconciliation line ("127 items verified"), an INFO "Stock updated for ITEM-1234 - new level: 42 units", an INFO "Order ORD-5678 processed - 3 units of ITEM-1234", an INFO "Inventory item ITEM-1234 checked - stock level: 45 units", and one WARN "Low stock warning for ITEM-9999 - current level: 5 units". No fault or alert is the subject of this request, so no cause is asserted; the log content observed is routine application activity and a single low-stock warning. All log evidence covers only the one-hour window ending 2026-11-23T18:50:46Z, and the observed stream begins at 18:50:11, so earlier logs are not in evidence.

claims.text: Namespace app-102 contained exactly two pods at query time: inventory-service-7ff7d5959f-vlqgl (phase Running, containers inventory-service and promtail) and loki-66445c6d6f-pj6sf (container loki).

fetch_pod_logs for inventory-service-7ff7d5959f-vlqgl in namespace app-102 over 2026-11-23T17:50:46Z to 2026-11-23T18:50:46Z returned 8 lines (source_start_at 2026-11-23T18:50:13.003Z, source_end_at 2026-11-23T18:50:18.103Z), all from the promtail sidecar: Promtail 2.9.0 start-up, config reload, "Adding target" key="/var/log/*.log:{job=\"inventory-service\", namespace=\"app-102\"}", and tail of /var/log/inventory.log.

In the same fetch_pod_logs call the inventory-service container's current stream reported 0 lines read and 0 bytes, and both containers' previous instances were reported unavailable (HTTP 400: previous terminated container not found), so no restarted/previous-container logs existed for this pod.

Loki query {job="inventory-service"} over 2026-11-23T17:50:46Z to 2026-11-23T18:50:46Z returned 8 application log lines from filename=/var/log/inventory.log, service=inventory-service, pod_name=inventory-service-7ff7d5959f-vlqgl, spanning 2026-11-23T18:50:11.885Z to 2026-11-23T18:50:44.414Z: INFO 'Inventory item ITEM-1234 checked - stock level: 45 units', INFO 'Order ORD-5678 processed - 3 units of ITEM-1234', INFO 'Stock updated for ITEM-1234 - new level: 42 units', WARN 'Low stock warning for ITEM-9999 - current level: 5 units', INFO 'Inventory reconciliation completed - 127 items verified', and three INFO 'Inventory check completed - all systems operational' lines at 18:50:24.397Z, 18:50:34.406Z and 18:50:44.414Z.

A namespace-wide Loki query {namespace="app-102"} for the same hour returned the same 8 lines from the inventory-service stream and nothing else (2 streams returned, source_start_at 2026-11-23T18:50:11.885Z, source_end_at 2026-11-23T18:50:44.414Z).

The inventory-service application does not write to container stdout/stderr in this pod; its logs are file-based at /var/log/inventory.log, which the promtail sidecar tails and ships to Loki, so Loki (not fetch_pod_logs) is the source for its application logs.

gaps: All log evidence covers only the one-hour window 2026-11-23T17:50:46Z to 2026-11-23T18:50:46Z, and the observed inventory-service log stream starts at 2026-11-23T18:50:11.885Z, so nothing before that instant was retrieved; log retention, node log rotation and the tool's window limit make earlier lines unknown.

The error-filtered Loki query {job="inventory-service"} |~ "(?i)error|fatal|panic|fail|exception" returned zero lines with status no_data (not citable as fact), so the absence of error lines in this window is unconfirmed rather than established.
The inventory-service container's own stdout stream returned 0 lines; whether it emitted output outside the sampled window or output that was never flushed to stdout is unknown.
No metric, trace or Kubernetes-event checks were performed for this pod; this Run only retrieved logs, so its availability/error signals were not assessed.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
